feature: ADR-0088 Linux paired clock continuity and latched native clock faults

linux.abi: GNU C checks MONOTONIC1/BOOTTIME7 and clock_gettime prototype plus prior ABI; no clock calls in oracle
linux.native: existing read-only reactor clock/wait and no-input native host/worker harnesses now use paired clocks

windows.scope: Linux-only change; prior portable CLI/native checks remain pending after automatic approval quota failure

limitations: CLOCK_MONOTONIC remains the event/deadline domain. BOOTTIME is evidence only, not substitute event timestamps or fabricated lease progress.
Every now samples mono-before/boot/mono-after; span<=10ms. Intersect signed offset intervals across the same run, accepting equality/negative namespace offsets.
Overlapping intervals can hide small offset changes; initial/current widths permit up to20ms ambiguity. This is not proof of no suspend.
Non-atomic sample-to-dispatch gap remains; suspend after sampling may occur before dispatch. Pre-suspend notification/inhibition and actual suspend/resume tests remain necessary.
First sample establishes baseline; no historical suspend evidence is inferred. New clock must not reauthorize existing runtime/provider.
Clock fault is permanent for the same object, preserves last accepted time/errno, no retry/alternate clock fallback. Fresh terminal-finalization clocks operate after runtime owners drop.
No system suspend/resume/time setting, VT/evdev/uinput, Hook/SendInput or driver operation performed. Native tests read clocks and owned no-input IPC only.
Kernel scheduling/syscall stalls can exceed sample width and cause conservative failure; native operations have no hard execution bound.
